newsitem.title: USA: Oakland, Calif., OKs $435 mln pension bond deal.
newsitem.headline: Oakland, Calif., OKs $435 mln pension bond deal.

text.p: The Oakland, Calif., city council approved a controversial $435 million financing for its pension fund, city officials said on Wednesday.

The financing was narrowly approved by the city council on Tuesday night. Proponents of the financing said it would save the city as much as $17 million over the next few years. Opponents of the plan said the refinancing was too risky.
Under the plan, the city would sell about $435 million of pension obligation bonds to fund a portion of the city's unfunded liability to its police and fire retirement system.
PaineWebber is lead underwriter on the deal, which could come to market next week, depending on market conditions, Janice Mazyck, Oakland's treasury manager, said.
"We're just waiting for the market to cooperate," she said.
